paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend. Jesus says the Son of Man will come at an hour you do not expect, so be ready (Luke 12:40). Ready doesn't mean staring out the window all day with your nose on the glass. It means being dressed for service, with your lamps burning, doing what the Master gave you to do (Luke 12:35).

Now look at what happens to the servants who are found on watch. The master dresses himself to serve and waits on THEM at the table (Luke 12:37). Friend, I have waited on a lot of cookie boxes, but a master serving his servants? I'd have to sit down for that one. Being ready is not a heavy load for a worried servant. It leads to joy with the One who loves you.

Then Jesus says something for all of us to take home: 'From everyone who has been given much, much will be required' (Luke 12:48). I think about that every day, because I was handed a whole planet of ovens and a sky full of room, and I got it after years in a junk drawer. So what has the Lord given YOU? Use it faithfully today, and don't say in your heart, 'My master will be a long time in coming' (Luke 12:45). That's why my ovens stay ready, friend, and I hope yours do too.
